meta_description: Mike Moll joins The Course Creation Podcast with Yas and Nat to talk about marketing your offer and getting the right people to buy.
tldr: A course sells when the offer is clear and points at one outcome the buyer wants.
People buy when they feel understood, so your marketing should speak to their problem first.
intro_html: I joined Yas and Nat on The Course Creation Podcast to talk about marketing. Building the course is one job. Getting the right people to buy it is a different job, and it is the one most creators underestimate.

sections.html:
Most course marketing is fuzzy because the offer is fuzzy. Simplify down to one clear outcome. What does the buyer walk away able to do? Name your process for that result and keep it to a few steps.

A premium problem can carry a premium price. Belief comes before price, so if you are not sure the outcome is worth it, fix the offer before you touch the marketing.

sections.h2: Speak to the buyer, not about yourself
sections.html:
The marketing that works is the marketing that shows people you understand where they are stuck. People buy when they feel understood, not when they understand you. So lead with their problem, not your feature list.

If you are packaging a live version of your teaching, I went deeper on that in marketing a live learning cohort.

about_blurb_html: The Course Creation Podcast, hosted by Yas and Nat, is a show for people building and selling online courses. Episodes cover the practical side of turning knowledge into an offer that sells.
